---
title: "10 · Buffer Overflow Lab"
---

## Setup

Install required packages:

```bash
sudo apt install gdb pip gcc-multilib
sudo apt install python3-pwntools
```

## Disable ASLR

Address Space Layout Randomization must be disabled for this demo to be predictable:

```bash
echo 0 | sudo tee /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space
```

## Part 1 — Basic Buffer Overflow

Create the following vulnerable program (`vulnerable.c`):

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

void vulnerable_function(char *input) {
    char buffer[64];
    strcpy(buffer, input);
    printf("Buffer content: %s\n", buffer);
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        printf("Usage: %s <input>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    vulnerable_function(argv[1]);
    return 0;
}
```

Compile (disabling stack protections):

```bash
gcc -fno-stack-protector -z execstack -no-pie -m32 -g vulnerable.c -o vulnerable
```

Run with normal input (safe):

```bash
./vulnerable "Hello Students"
```

Trigger the overflow — this causes a segmentation fault:

```bash
./vulnerable $(python -c 'print "A" * 100')
```

## Part 2 — Weaponizing the Overflow

New vulnerable program with `setuid` (`vulnerable_root.c`):

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

void vulnerable_function(char *input) {
    char buffer[64];
    strcpy(buffer, input);
    printf("Buffer content: %s\n", buffer);
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        printf("Usage: %s <input>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    setuid(0);
    vulnerable_function(argv[1]);
    return 0;
}
```

Compile:

```bash
gcc -fno-stack-protector -z execstack -no-pie -m32 -g vulnerable_root.c -o vulnerable_root
```

## Find the Buffer Offset

Use `pwntools` cyclic patterns to find the exact offset:

```bash
python3 -c 'from pwn import *; print(cyclic_find(0x6161616c))'
```

Use GDB to locate EIP and confirm the offset:

```bash
gdb -q ./vulnerable_root
(gdb) run $(python -c 'print "A" * 100')
# Note the segmentation fault and check EIP
# Adjust the input size until you find the exact offset
```
